lines.text: And it sprang fully formed from your head, like a Greek goddess?

No, no. Long road. In January I made ARIA, a chat that keeps thinking in the background on a local Llama. Two days later it became AutoClawd. Always-on mic, your screen, a small local model. Two hundred and seventy-one commits. And it got big. A pixel world, camera, face, gestures, a call mode.

lines.text: So I built video2ai. It downloads the video, and instead of watching it frame by frame, it runs a pass of the transcript, figures out what's being said, the music, the sound effects. Then it uses Apple's own machine learning to see how the frames change, makes a timestamped grid of the frames, and puts it all into HTML.

Okay. Frame selection is a vector math problem, not an LLM problem. Apple's engine, already on your Mac, gives each frame a fingerprint, and you keep only the ones where the picture actually changed. A video goes from about a hundred and seventy thousand tokens to about a hundred and fifty lines. Way faster, way more effective, and easy to give references.

Therapy by doodle. I have paid good money for less.

lines.text: And why the nineties? Not that I am complaining. I peaked in the nineties.

Everyone's building with the same model intelligence now, so the average looks the same. So I tried to differentiate on every aspect. A CV becomes a CD. A portfolio becomes an app. The app becomes a podcast. And you get to steer it.
